subject: Private runtime instantiation questionnaire — operator boundaries & upgrade window
messages:
From: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@edgenet.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@edgenet.com>, EdgeNet Procurement <procure@edgenet.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment questionnaire — operator boundary clarification

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the questionnaire you sent. We are reviewing the operator responsibilities section and need clarification on a couple of points before we submit this to our security team:

1) You indicate "operator accounts are separated from runtime host accounts" — can you confirm whether operator credentials are scoped per-customer (unique to each EdgeNet install) or if there is any shared operator identity across customer deployments?

2) During maintenance windows you mention an optional "upgrade assist" mode. For our procurement SOW we need to know what access (SSH or remote console) your operators would request, whether they require ephemeral credentials, and if those actions are auditable within the customer's local telemetry.

Could you provide a short matrix showing responsibilities and the exact artifacts you produce (runbooks, signed attestations, keystore handoff notes)? If possible, attach any sample matrices or a short playbook excerpt.

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Torres
Senior Security Engineer, EdgeNet

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@edgenet.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questionnaire — operator boundary clarification

Hi Alicia,

Thanks — great questions. Below is a high-level answer and I attached a short artifacts matrix and our maintenance playbook excerpt for reference. Full evidence can be shared under an NDA if needed.

Summary answers (short):
- Operator identities: per-customer. We provision operator accounts scoped to the customer's tenant and local operator roles are instantiated in the private control plane you host. There is no shared operator identity across customers.
- Maintenance/upgrade access: two modes — "self-service" (customer runs the provided upgrade bundle using operators' runbook) and "assist" (Redwood operator performs limited actions). For assist we use ephemeral, customer-logged accounts that expire after the session. Actions require both a timebound access grant from the customer's admin and multi-factor confirmation from our SRE.
- Auditing: all assist sessions generate a signed session record written to local telemetry and to the deploy's syslog/ELK endpoint. We include hashes of the session transcript in our audit artifact.

Attachments included: operator_boundaries_matrix.xlsx (mapping of actions/roles), upgrade_maintenance_playbook.pdf (playbook excerpt), and a short text file describing our KMS integration pattern.

I'll paste a compact matrix below for quick context and Vanessa/Laura can add ops-level specifics.

--- compact matrix (summary) ---
Operator role: Redwoods-Assist-Operator
Can: trigger upgrade, tail logs, run validation smoke tests, escalate to local admin
Cannot: export customer keystore, retrieve plaintext model artifacts, reconfigure network egress rules
Required artifact: ephemeral-access-token, signed access grant, session transcript stored locally

Operator role: Customer-Operator
Can: full install, keystore handoff, routine patching, approve assist sessions
Cannot: access Redwood tenant control plane (no global admin)
Required artifact: operator handoff checklist, operator identity cert (x509)

--- end matrix ---

If you want, Vanessa can schedule a quick 30m walkthrough of the playbook and how the ephemeral access flow ties into your SIEM.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment questionnaire — operator boundary clarification

Rishi / Vanessa,

This is helpful. A couple follow-ups from our security reviewer:

- For the ephemeral-access-token mechanism, can you confirm the token issuer and where the signing keys are stored? We cannot accept tokens whose signing keys are not under our control for installs where we manage KMS.
- Can you provide a sample signed session record (redacted) and indicate the TTL for session transcripts in the local telemetry? EdgeNet requires a minimum 365-day retention for audit records.
- For the keystore handoff, do you support an HSM-backed import flow (we use an on-prem HSM) or do you require us to hand over plain key material?

If you can reply with short answers and the sample record by EOD Friday we'll move this into the procurement review.

Thanks — Tom
VP, Infrastructure & Security, EdgeNet

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Hayes <t.hayes@edgenet.com>, Alicia Torres <alicia.torres@edgenet.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 13:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment questionnaire — operator boundary clarification

Tom / Alicia — quick answers below, then I attached a redacted example of a signed session record and our KMS integration pattern.

1) Token issuer & signing keys: For private installs that manage their own KMS, the token signing key can be generated and stored in the customer's HSM/KMS. We provide the token-issuing service as a containerized component that you deploy inside the VPC. The service consumes a key reference from your KMS; signing never leaves your HSM. If you prefer Redwood-managed signing, we operate a fully audited CA in a segregated partition — but that's only for hosted/dedicated installs.

2) Session record sample & TTL: Attached is a redacted signed session record (JSON with signature). By default our install template sets local telemetry retention to 365 days; this is configurable per-customer. The session record includes: operator id, start/end timestamps, action list, hash of commands executed, and a signature.

3) HSM-backed keystore import: Yes — we support an HSM-backed import flow. You can either (a) import keys via an HSM-backed CSR flow where keys never leave your HSM, or (b) if you prefer operator-assisted rotation, we use an encrypted key-wrapping protocol with documented attestation steps. Plain key handoff is not required and is discouraged.

Next steps: I can convert the attachments into an SOW appendix and send a short redline that makes retention, token control, and HSM import explicit. Marissa — can you add a procurement-friendly paragraph for the SOW appendix that Tom can paste into their internal doc?

Vanessa
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

Tom / Alicia — attaching a short SOW appendix paragraph you can paste into your internal procurement language. Key points made explicit: token signing under customer KMS control, 365-day telemetry retention (configurable), HSM-backed import supported, and operator assist requires explicit one-time admin grant with an auditable session.

SOW appendix (proposed language):
"Redwood Inference will deliver the private runtime as a customer-hosted control plane packaged container image. All cryptographic signing material for ephemeral access tokens will be generated and stored in the customer's on-prem KMS/HSM. Redwood will provide a token-issuer component that runs inside the customer's VPC and references the customer's key material using standard KMS key references. All operator assist sessions will be executed using ephemeral, timebound credentials provisioned by the customer's KMS. Session transcripts and audit artifacts will be stored locally in the customer's telemetry stack for a minimum of 365 days; retention can be extended per customer policy. HSM-backed import flows are supported and preferred; plaintext key export is not required."
If that fits, we're happy to include it in the SOW and proceed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
